items.front: In Amazon EFS, one file system can have {{c1::1 mount target}} in each Availability Zone.
In Amazon EFS, a client mounts the file system by connecting to the {{c1::NFS port (TCP port 2049)}} of a mount target.
items.extra: A client [can only mount a file system](../facts/efs.md#efs-nfs-client-needs-network-connection-to-port-2049) if it can open a network connection to this port. The security group of the mount target decides that.

items.front: In Amazon EFS, a lifecycle policy with default settings moves a file from EFS Standard to EFS IA after {{c1::30 days}} without access.
In Amazon EFS, data in the EFS Archive storage class has a {{c1::minimum storage duration of 90 days}}.
items.extra: EFS IA has [no minimum storage duration](../facts/efs.md#efs-faq-archive-minimum-duration-90-days).

items.front: In EFS Replication, after the first sync, most file systems keep a recovery point objective {{c1::(RPO) of 15 minutes}}.
items.extra: The value holds [for most file systems](../facts/efs.md#efs-replication-rpo-15-minutes-most-file-systems), not for every file system.

items.front: In Amazon EFS, Elastic throughput fits applications that drive on average {{c1::5% or less of the peak throughput}}.
items.extra: Elastic throughput also fits [spiky or unpredictable workloads](../facts/efs.md#efs-elastic-best-for-spiky-low-average-to-peak).

items.front: In FSx for Windows File Server, a Multi-AZ failover to the standby file server typically completes in {{c1::less than 30 seconds}}.
In FSx for Windows File Server, the maximum storage capacity of one file system is {{c1::64 TiB}}.
In Amazon EFS, can Windows-based EC2 instances mount a file system?
items.back: No. Use FSx for Windows File Server.
items.extra: Amazon EFS with Windows-based EC2 instances [is not supported](../facts/efs.md#efs-windows-ec2-not-supported). FSx for Windows File Server gives [fully managed Microsoft Windows file servers](../facts/fsx.md#fsx-windows-fully-managed-native-windows-file-servers-smb).

items.front: In Amazon EFS, can you turn on encryption at rest for an existing unencrypted file system?
items.back: No. Create an encrypted file system and copy the data.
items.extra: After you create a file system, you [cannot change its encryption setting](../facts/efs.md#efs-encryption-setting-cannot-change-after-creation).

items.front: Linux instances in several Availability Zones need one shared file system, LEAST operational overhead. Which AWS service?
items.back: Amazon EFS, a Regional file system.
items.extra: Instances in several Availability Zones of one Region can use one EFS file system [concurrently from multiple NFS clients](../facts/efs.md#efs-concurrent-access-multiple-clients-multiple-azs).

items.front: Windows SMB file shares that use Active Directory permissions, fully managed. Which AWS file service?
items.back: FSx for Windows File Server.
items.extra: You [join it to your Active Directory domain](../facts/fsx.md#fsx-windows-joins-active-directory-for-authentication-and-acls), which gives user authentication and file- and folder-level access control.

items.front: High performance computing or machine learning jobs need fast file access to data in an S3 bucket. Which AWS file service?
items.back: FSx for Lustre, linked to the bucket.
items.extra: A linked FSx for Lustre file system [transparently presents S3 objects as files](../facts/fsx.md#fsx-lustre-s3-presents-objects-as-files-and-writes-back).

items.front: In Amazon EFS, Elastic or Provisioned throughput: which fits spiky, unpredictable workloads?
items.back: Elastic throughput.
items.extra: Elastic throughput is the best mode for [spiky or unpredictable workloads](../facts/efs.md#efs-elastic-best-for-spiky-low-average-to-peak).

items.front: NFS and SMB clients must use the same data, and the company runs NetApp storage today. Which Amazon FSx file system?
items.back: FSx for NetApp ONTAP.
items.extra: FSx for NetApp ONTAP supports [multi-protocol access](../facts/fsx.md#fsx-faq-ontap-nfs-smb-multiprotocol): NFS and SMB access to the same data at the same time.

items.front: A company moves its ZFS file servers to AWS and keeps its snapshot and clone workflow. Which AWS file service?
items.back: FSx for OpenZFS.
items.extra: AWS recommends [FSx for OpenZFS](../facts/fsx.md#fsx-when-to-choose-openzfs-from-zfs) when your current storage technology is ZFS or another Linux-based file server.

items.front: In Amazon EFS, Regional or One Zone: which file system type is designed to survive the loss of an Availability Zone?
items.back: Regional.
items.extra: Regional file systems are designed to [sustain data if an AZ is lost](../facts/efs.md#efs-regional-designed-to-sustain-az-loss).

items.front: In FSx for Lustre, scratch or persistent: which deployment type replicates data and replaces failed file servers?
items.back: Persistent.
items.extra: In a persistent file system, [data is replicated](../facts/fsx.md#fsx-lustre-persistent-replicated-servers-replaced) and [file servers are replaced if they fail](../facts/fsx.md#fsx-lustre-persistent-replicated-servers-replaced).

items.front: In FSx for Windows File Server, can the file system use AD Connector or Simple AD?
items.back: No. Use AWS Managed Microsoft AD or a self-managed AD.
items.extra: [Amazon FSx does not support](../facts/fsx.md#fsx-windows-ad-connector-simple-ad-not-supported) AD Connector and Simple AD. You can join an [existing, self-managed Active Directory domain](../facts/fsx.md#fsx-windows-ad-options-aws-managed-or-self-managed) or AWS Managed Microsoft AD.

items.front: In FSx for Windows File Server, can you decrease the storage capacity of a file system?
items.back: No. Storage capacity can grow but not shrink.
items.extra: Storage capacity is [Increase only](../facts/fsx.md#fsx-windows-storage-capacity-increase-only-never-decrease).

items.front: In EFS Replication, can an application write to the destination file system while replication is enabled?
items.back: No. The destination file system is read-only.
items.extra: Replication creates a [new read-only destination file system](../facts/efs.md#efs-replication-destination-read-only-while-replicating). To fail over, delete the replication configuration.

items.front: In Amazon EFS, can a file system use Max I/O performance mode with Elastic throughput?
items.back: No. Use General Purpose mode.
items.extra: Max I/O is not supported for [file systems that use Elastic throughput](../facts/efs.md#efs-max-io-not-supported-one-zone-or-elastic), and it is [not supported for One Zone file systems](../facts/efs.md#efs-max-io-not-supported-one-zone-or-elastic).

items.front: In Amazon EFS, does a lifecycle policy with default settings move a file in EFS IA back to EFS Standard when someone reads it?
items.back: No. Set Transition into Standard on first access.
items.extra: By default, files are [not moved back to the Standard storage class](../facts/efs.md#efs-lifecycle-default-no-move-back-to-standard) when they are accessed.

items.front: In Amazon EFS, files are read a few times a year or less and must stay on the file system, MOST cost-effective. Which storage class?
items.back: EFS Archive.
items.extra: EFS Archive is designed for data accessed [a few times a year or less](../facts/efs.md#efs-faq-ia-quarter-archive-year-designed-for).

items.front: In FSx for Lustre, can you back up a scratch file system?
items.back: No. Scratch file systems are for temporary storage.
items.extra: [Backups aren’t supported on scratch file systems](../facts/fsx.md#fsx-faq-lustre-backups-not-on-scratch), because scratch is for temporary storage.

items.front: In FSx for Lustre linked to S3, must the whole bucket be copied before a job can start?
items.back: No. A file's content loads on first access.
items.extra: The content of an object is [imported automatically from S3 only when you access](../facts/fsx.md#fsx-faq-lustre-s3-object-imported-on-first-access) the file.

items.front: In FSx for Windows File Server, Single-AZ or Multi-AZ: which fails over to a standby file server in another zone?
items.back: Multi-AZ.
items.extra: A Multi-AZ file system has [a preferred AZ and a standby AZ](../facts/fsx.md#fsx-windows-multi-az-standby-two-azs-sync-replication), with data replicated synchronously.

items.front: In FSx for Windows File Server, SQL Server needs highly available SMB shares across Availability Zones. Which setup?
items.back: A Multi-AZ file system with continuously available shares.
items.extra: For SQL Server you [use CA shares on Multi-AZ file systems](../facts/fsx.md#fsx-windows-ca-shares-required-multi-az-for-sql-server).

items.front: In FSx for NetApp ONTAP, which tiering policy moves cold user data and snapshots to capacity pool storage?
items.back: Auto.
items.extra: Under Auto, the cooling period [by default is 31 days](../facts/fsx.md#fsx-ontap-tiering-policy-auto-31-days-default-console).

items.front: In FSx for NetApp ONTAP SnapLock Compliance mode, can any user delete a WORM file during its retention period?
items.back: No. Not even an administrator.
items.extra: A file in WORM state [cannot be modified or deleted by any user](../facts/fsx.md#fsx-faq-ontap-snaplock-compliance-no-delete) during its retention period.

items.front: In Amazon EFS, on-premises Linux servers must mount the file system. Which connection to the VPC do they need?
items.back: AWS Direct Connect or Site-to-Site VPN.
items.extra: On-premises servers mount EFS when they connect to the VPC with [AWS Direct Connect or Site-to-Site VPN](../facts/efs.md#efs-onpremises-mount-via-direct-connect-or-vpn).

items.front: In Amazon EFS, mount target or access point: which one enforces a user identity and a root directory?
items.back: An access point.
items.extra: An access point can [enforce a user identity](../facts/efs.md#efs-access-point-enforces-posix-user-and-root-directory) and [enforce a different root directory](../facts/efs.md#efs-access-point-enforces-posix-user-and-root-directory).
